external_entities.name: Member
external_entities.description: A library member using the library app to borrow, renew and reserve books.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members borrow, renew and reserve books through the library app on their phones.

external_entities.name: Desk staff
external_entities.description: Library desk staff who manually extend loans, clear account blocks and mark books as returned.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Desk staff can extend a loan, clear a block on a member's account or mark a book as returned by hand
external_entities.notes: Everyone at the desk uses the same shared login; individual staff and branch cannot be identified from the history.

processes.name: Library app
processes.description: A phone application through which members borrow, renew and reserve books.
processes.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API.

processes.name: Lending API
processes.description: The REST API that is the service interface for loans and serves the circulation page.
processes.source_excerpt: It's a REST API. JSON in, JSON out.
processes.notes: The written note says the lending API is internal-only, while the interview says phones talk straight to it over the internet. The two claims conflict, so exposure is unknown.

processes.name: Self-service kiosk
processes.description: A branch kiosk where a member scans their library card and books being borrowed or returned.
processes.source_excerpt: The kiosks are in every branch and they send each loan and each return to the lending API as it is scanned.
processes.notes: The interview does not establish what the kiosks talk to other than what arrives at the lending API.

data_stores.name: Loans database
data_stores.description: The single database containing members, loans and reservations, including member contact details and full borrowing history.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Names, email addresses, home addresses and every member's full borrowing history live in the loans database.
data_stores.notes: The interview corrects the earlier reference to two databases: it states that they were merged into one loans database and that the old reservations database is gone.

data_flows.name: borrow books
data_flows.description: A member uses the library app to borrow, renew or reserve books.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members borrow, renew and reserve books through the library app on their phones.
data_flows.data_description: Book and member requests for borrowing, renewing and reserving

data_flows.name: change loans
data_flows.description: The library app calls the lending API with member and book or title information to borrow, renew or reserve.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API. It says which book and which member, and the API checks the loan rules and writes the change.
data_flows.notes: Authentication is unknown. Priya said: "I think it checks a token the app gets at sign-in, but I'd have to look." She also said she could not tell what the API accepts or does with a call it does not like.
data_flows.data_description: Member and book or title information for borrowing, renewing and reserving

data_flows.name: send loan records
data_flows.description: A kiosk sends each loan and return to the lending API as it is scanned.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The kiosks send each loan and each return to the lending API.
data_flows.data_description: Loan and return records, including scanned member and book information

data_flows.name: update loans
data_flows.description: Desk staff use the circulation page served by the lending API to extend loans, clear account blocks and mark books returned.
data_flows.source_excerpt: someone at the desk opens the circulation page and marks it returned, or clears the block on the account.
data_flows.notes: The circulation page uses one shared login. The password is on a card taped under the desk, and the history records only that the loan was closed by hand.

data_flows.name: read-write records
data_flows.description: The lending API reads and writes member, loan and reservation records in the loans database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The API is the only thing that reads or writes it.
data_flows.data_description: Members, loans, reservations and member borrowing history

trust_boundaries.name: Member phone
trust_boundaries.description: The phone environment on which the library app runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API.

trust_boundaries.name: Branch network
trust_boundaries.description: The network used by branch kiosks and desk staff.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The kiosks sit on the branch network.

trust_boundaries.name: Council data centre
trust_boundaries.description: The council data-centre environment where the lending API and loans database run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The lending API and the loans database run in the council data centre.

assumptions.assumption: The member phone is a tenant-controlled zone because the app is described as running on the member's phone.
assumptions.basis: The source says the library app is on the member's phone; a member-controlled device is a different party's environment.

assumptions.assumption: The lending API presents a web interface because it is explicitly described as a REST API.
assumptions.basis: The source states: "It's a REST API. JSON in, JSON out." REST is a web application interface under the model's interface classification.

assumptions.assumption: The loans database contains confidential data because it stores names, email addresses, home addresses and full member borrowing history.
assumptions.basis: The interview explicitly lists personal names, email addresses, home addresses and borrowing history as contents of the database.
